corrections.caveats: The benchmark treats the two sides unequally. The custom side runs ./bench with one untimed warm-up call and then one timed call on already-allocated, already-touched buffers (C is zeroed once before the warm-up and not re-zeroed; utils/bench.c). The baseline times a single NumPy A @ B call in a fresh Python process with no warm-up and with the result matrix allocated inside the timed region (scripts/openblas.py). There is one measurement per n, no repeats or variance, the metric is 'largest n within a cumulative time budget' rather than GFLOPS, and the custom code is built with -ffast-math. The README does not say which NumPy or OpenBLAS build was used; because OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 changes the baseline curve and the implied single-thread rate is about 110 GFLOPS, the baseline was evidently a NEON-path OpenBLAS rather than Apple Accelerate (inferred, not stated). OpenBLAS issue #6073 (2026-09-29, Apple M4 Pro, OpenBLAS develop 63d7f22) reports 707-766 GFLOPS single-thread OpenBLAS SGEMM and 1127-1185 GFLOPS for Accelerate, so the platform's fastest BLAS (Accelerate/SME) and SME-enabled OpenBLAS were not compared and would likely beat this NEON code by a wide margin. Parity is the only single-thread result, and the author attributes the multi-thread gap to load balancing on his particular M4, which may be a P/E-core scheduling artifact. Numbers are read by eye from the plot image. The author's deep-dive post on ninjadenmu.github.io is egress-blocked. No license (no LICENSE file, none in the GitHub sidebar).
